Outcome_variable.evidence_source: Our results demonstrated that while there were significant and relatively large differences between dropouts and graduates in depressive symptoms and life satisfaction at T1, even after controlling for demographic variables, by 4 years later these differences had decreased. After controlling for demographic variables, we found that the differences between high school graduates and dropouts in T3 depressive symptoms and life satisfaction became insignificant.

sample_type.evidence_source: The purpose of this study was to examine mental health during emerging adulthood among a cohort of high school graduates and dropouts. [...] The authors gratefully acknowledge the Boston area high schools, adolescents, and parents who participated in this study.

ethnicity.evidence_source: This section does not report the ethnic composition of the sample.

lag.evidence_source: This study adds to past studies that explored the effects of dropping out (e.g., Kaplan et al. 1994; Kortering et al. 1997; Ou 2008), by extending the period of observation over 4 years. Our results demonstrated that while there were significant and relatively large differences between dropouts and graduates in depressive symptoms and life satisfaction at T1, even after controlling for demographic variables, by 4 years later these differences had decreased. [...] we found that the differences between high school graduates and dropouts in T3 depressive symptoms and life satisfaction became insignificant.
lag.warning: The study observed participants over 4 years from T1 to T3, implying two intervals. Assuming equal intervals, the lag is 4 years / 2 intervals = 2.0 years.
